children: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) is accelerating AI and data‑center growth—projecting a $2T–$3T AI TAM by 2030, targeting ~$70B data‑center revenue and low‑$40B AI GPU sales, while expanding supply via $29–30B commitments, new Threadripper Halo Station gear, strategic partnerships and funding tied to chip deployments.
: AMD CFO Jean Hu projected an AI TAM of about $2T–$3T by 2030. Company sees data-center revenue ~ $70B by 2027, AI GPUs ~ low-$40B; strong CPU/GPU demand and planned CPU supply increase.
: AMD says supply chain limits: advanced wafers, HB memory and packaging constrained. Company has $29–30B in purchase commitments to boost production.
: AMD is a named hardware partner in Backline, an open-source platform integrated into Xanadu’s PennyLane, enabling low-latency classical-to-quantum integration using AMD CPUs, GPUs and FPGAs.

: AMD shares rose ~6% Tuesday and climbed in after-hours after CFO Jean Hu outlined an accelerated expansion plan at the Citi Global TMT Conference, signaling investor appetite for the growth strategy.
: AMD launched the Threadripper Halo Station: 96‑core Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9995WX, dual liquid‑cooled Instinct MI350P GPUs (expandable to 4), and 288–576 GB HBM3E — for local large AI models.
: AMD helped fund a $300M loan to AI infra startup Crusoe, tied to Crusoe deploying AMD chips to expand use of AMD processors in AI infrastructure.
This is an AI-generated summary and may contain inaccuracies. Please verify any important information with the original sources.

title: Weekly Recap: AI TAM $2T–$3T by 2030 and supply constraints with $29–30B commitments
